amendment: Before any reservoir outcome access, live proof found nine point-in-time defects. Two early windows discarded separately captured WebSocket flow during REST execution fallback; the next used exchange clocks rather than local receipt clocks for spot freshness; the next exposed long SQLite-cadence gaps in the legacy spot-mid path; the next missed its delayed RTI deadline during rollback-journal contention; the first WAL window exposed synchronous optional shadow scoring; the next exposed serial strategy-ledger writes in the exact worker; the next exposed queued-old Coinbase updates; the next proved that even asynchronous same-process ledger writes starved both spot providers; and the first durable-spool window proved that repeated full health-graph requests after 13M could themselves starve the providers before +30s. All affected windows are excluded by moving the prospective boundary forward. Delayed evidence is hash-bound into a separate WAL spool immediately after capture and cannot enter the heavy strategy ledger until 95 seconds after 13M. The spool is restart-durable, idempotent, tamper-detecting, outcome-free, and recovery respects its intervals. Full health reconstruction is now prohibited from 75 seconds before 13M through 100 seconds after it; requests receive the last immutable cached snapshot during the entire evidence/spool-release window. The local restart guard covers the same post-capture interval. The native spot sampler, incremental Coinbase books, independent source-clock gate, persistent quote pool, and optional-shadow deferral remain required. Frozen controls remain unchanged and no historical values are backfilled.
objective: retain point-in-time 12-minute Kalshi and spot microstructure already captured by the exact collector so future reversal models can be trained and tested without reconstructing or backfilling evidence
